name: Spencer Morley Consulting
description: Canadian consulting firm with two practice areas: (1) Crisis communications for governments, school boards, and organizations across Alberta — led by Cheryl Spencer-Morley, 25+ years senior public sector communications; (2) AI consulting for Canadian municipalities (all provinces), Alberta small businesses, and non-profits across Canada — led by Jordan Morley, Google AI Professional Certificate. Contact: jordan@spencermorleyconsulting.ca

tools.name: general-consultation-request
tools.description: Request a consultation about AI consulting or strategic communications services. Spencer Morley Consulting serves Canadian municipalities on AI governance and Alberta businesses on AI adoption and visibility.

tools.name: municipal-ai-consultation
tools.description: Request a consultation about municipal AI compliance, shadow AI governance, Privacy Management Program requirements (ATIA/POPA in Alberta, FOIPPA in BC, MFIPPA in Ontario), AI policy development, staff training, or private LLM deployment. SMC serves small and rural municipalities across all Canadian provinces remotely. Entry point: Municipal AI Readiness Assessment.

tools.name: small-business-ai-consultation
tools.description: Request AI consulting for a small business in Edmonton or across Alberta. This is a distinct small-business practice, not an extension of SMC's municipal work. Covers AI workflow audits, an AI adoption roadmap for Alberta SMBs, staff AI adoption and training, operational efficiency, and workflow automation for quoting, bookings, lead handling, customer service and sales admin — plus AI search visibility (AEO/GEO/webMCP). Industries served: professional services, construction and trades, accounting, manufacturing, retail. Two entry points: (1) Staff AI Risk Review — an internal AI use and risk review, $600 CAD, credited toward any follow-on service; (2) Discoverability Index — free quick check, or the Discoverability Report at $1,500, credited in full against the Fix Sprint.

tools.name: non-profit-ai-consultation
tools.description: Request a consultation about safe and ethical AI use for non-profits across Canada. SMC helps mission-driven organizations adopt AI in a clear progression: (1) ethical and safe AI training for staff working with donor, client, and case data, delivered with a plain-language AI use policy for board adoption; (2) systems and workflow automation for receipting, grant and funder reporting, intake, and scheduling; (3) a private, local LLM that runs on hardware the organization controls so sensitive data never leaves the building — the non-profit counterpart to SMC's private municipal AI. Entry point: a no-cost AI Readiness Conversation.

tools.name: crisis-communications-consultation
tools.description: Request crisis communications support, media relations training, fractional/interim Public Information Officer (PIO) staffing, or municipal rebrand and website development for Alberta governments, school boards, municipalities, or organizations. Led by Cheryl Spencer-Morley — 25+ years federal, provincial, and municipal government communications, including embedded crisis-response work for the Municipality of Jasper during its 2024 wildfire response and a full rebrand and website delivered for the County of Minburn. Services: crisis planning, real-time response support, media training, on-demand communications counsel, fractional PIO services, municipal rebrand and website development.

tools.name: discoverability-index-audit
tools.description: Request a Discoverability Index (SDI) — a done-for-you audit measuring whether AI search and classical search send customers to a business or to its competitors. SMC runs live queries across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Copilot, verifies the website by live browser render, scores the business 0-100 across four areas (classical SEO, AI visibility/AEO-GEO, webMCP readiness, Canadian trust signals), ranks it against 7-10 named local competitors on a leaderboard, models the revenue at stake, and delivers a 90-day roadmap. Pricing (CAD): Discoverability Report $1,500 (scan + report), credited in full against the Fix Sprint; Report + Fix Sprint $3,900 (report plus implementation of the fixes); Discoverability Monitoring $400/month (quarterly re-score and ongoing monitoring, 3-month minimum). Distinct from the self-serve Staff AI Risk Review, which is an internal AI-readiness self-assessment.

tools.name: municipal-resident-survey-request
tools.description: Request a conversation about running a resident or community survey for a Canadian municipality, including the security assessment, privacy review and What We Heard reporting.

Plus Staff Training, Workflow Automation, and Website Design & AEO/SEO/GEO/WebMCP Readiness.

Entry point: a no-cost AI Readiness Conversation.

resources.name: BC Municipality AI Guide
resources.description: FOIPPA obligations for BC municipalities including Section 30.1 data residency requirements.

resources.name: Ontario Municipality AI Guide
resources.description: MFIPPA obligations for Ontario municipalities including IPC Ontario AI guidance and Privacy Impact Assessment requirements.

resources.name: AI Visibility Guide Series
resources.description: Four-part educational series: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization), AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), SEO in the AI Era, and WebMCP Explained — all focused on helping Alberta businesses get found and recommended by AI platforms.

resources.name: Discoverability Index (SDI)
resources.description: Product page for the Discoverability Index: a 0-100 score of how findable and recommendable a business is across AI search and classical search, scored against 7-10 named competitors on a leaderboard, with dollars-at-stake modelling and a prioritized 90-day roadmap. Tiers (CAD): Discoverability Report $1,500 (credited in full against the Fix Sprint), Report + Fix Sprint $3,900, Discoverability Monitoring $400/mo. Includes a full anonymized sample report.

resources.name: Data Security & Residency
resources.description: How Spencer Morley Consulting secures client and resident data: its client-facing tools, including online resident survey programs for Alberta municipalities, run on OVHcloud VPS infrastructure hosted in Beauharnois, Quebec (Canada). Documents the ISO 27001-certified data center infrastructure, Canadian data residency relevant to ATIA/POPA/FOIPPA/MFIPPA, and the shared-responsibility split between OVHcloud and SMC.

resources.name: Case Studies — Experience & Approach
resources.description: Named client case studies and the experience behind SMC's two practice areas. Includes the Municipality of Jasper's 2024 wildfire response (Cheryl Spencer-Morley served as Lead Crisis Communications Consultant, roughly two and a half months embedded on the ground, effectively functioning as the municipality's Public Information Officer and communications liaison — independently corroborated by CatIQ Connect's speaker profile), County of Grande Prairie No. 1 (crisis communications plan, internal communications plan, and staff training), County of Minburn (full rebrand and website, resident surveys, Agricultural Service Board strategic plan facilitation, land use bylaw communications, emergency management training), and the Ratio Strategy digital brand launch (Next.js website with SEO/AEO/GEO/WebMCP implementation).

resources.name: Resident Surveys for Canadian Municipalities
resources.description: Service page for municipal resident and community surveys: survey instrument design, a written four-layer security assessment before go-live, a requirement-by-requirement privacy review against Alberta's Protection of Privacy Act, hosting on the municipality's own subdomain on Canadian infrastructure, a staff administration portal, thematic analysis, and a written What We Heard report with a verbatim appendix. Includes the County of Minburn case study.
